answer: Persistent-Work Identity Ledger. Each identity must periodically forge a signed provenance record chaining its prior outputs; the ledger only accepts records whose history spans a minimum continuous window. To spin up N clones, an attacker must run N parallel work histories for that full window, since idle or pre-generated chains fail a timestamped raven audit that samples random past intervals. The karst of accumulated compute and elapsed attention is the barrier: cost scales with identities times window length, not with a one-time fee.
